steps.name: DESeq2 Wald test with apeglm shrinkage, plus edgeR QL as robustness check
caveats: With 3 replicates per group, both DESeq2 and edgeR have low power: expect to recover only a minority of true DE genes, skewed toward large fold changes. A gene absent from the significant list is not evidence it is unchanged. Do not loosen the FDR threshold to compensate.
Treat the DESeq2/edgeR intersection as the higher-confidence gene set; report method-only genes as a secondary, lower-confidence set — do not report the union as 'the' DE gene list

Reactome and Hallmark gene sets overlap in content; do not present overlapping hits from the two collections as independent confirmatory findings

plan.title: Liver drug treatment vs control DE + robustness + pathways
plan.analytical_narrative: The dataset is 3 treated vs 3 control human liver samples (raw Salmon gene-level counts, 12000 genes x 6 samples, single batch, unpaired). At n=3 per group the design has real but limited power, so the plan is built to answer both halves of the question: which genes differ, and how much can we trust that list. Step 1 runs sample-structure QC (blind VST, PCA, sample-distance heatmap, library sizes) to confirm the 6 samples cluster by condition and to catch an outlier or mislabel before any test is fit — with only 3 replicates per group, a single bad sample would dominate the result. Step 2 fits the primary DESeq2 Wald test (median-of-ratios normalization, minimal pre-filter, apeglm-shrunken log2FC, BH-adjusted independent filtering at alpha=0.05), and in the same step also fits edgeR quasi-likelihood as an orthogonal second method on the identical counts and design, because published benchmarks show DESeq2 and edgeR calls diverge more at low replicate counts, so the intersection of the two gives a higher-confidence gene set than either alone. Step 3 takes the DESeq2 Wald statistic (chosen ranking metric, stated per the disputed-rule requirement) and runs preranked fgsea against MSigDB Hallmark, then Reactome, on the full tested gene list rather than a p-value cutoff, since a discrete significant list at n=3 is expected to be short and underpowered for over-representation testing. Step 4 assembles the report: gene tables (unshrunken and shrunken LFC, SE, padj), diagnostic plots (MA, dispersion, p-value histogram), the DESeq2/edgeR overlap as the high-confidence gene set, an explicit statement of the expected power at n=3 replicates (most true DE genes with large fold changes are detected; smaller effects and an absent gene from the list are not evidence of no change), and the enrichment results with leading-edge genes and full reproducibility record (session info, package versions, gene-set collection versions).
